arxiv-2105-07000.title: Impacts of Water Latent Heat on the Thermal Structure of Ultra-Cool Objects: Brown Dwarfs and Free-Floating Planets Journal: ApJ astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , PICASO ( Batalha et al. 2019 ; Batalha & Rooney 2020 ) , Pandeia ( Pontoppidan et al. 2016 )
arxiv-2105-07000.creator: Shih-Yun Tang, Tyler D. Robinson, Mark S. Marley, Natasha E. Batalha, Roxana Lupu, L. Prato
arxiv-2105-07000.description: Abstract Brown dwarfs are essential targets for understanding planetary and sub-stellar atmospheres across a wide range of thermal and chemical conditions. As surveys continue to probe ever deeper, and as observing capabilities continue to improve, the number of known Y dwarfs — the coldest class of sub-stellar objects, with effective temperatures below about 600 K — is rapidly growing.

arxiv-2202-09327.title: Hadamard Inverse Function Theorem Proved by Variational Analysis
arxiv-2202-09327.creator: Milen Ivanov, Nadia Zlateva
arxiv-2202-09327.description: Abstract We present a proof of Hadamard Inverse Function Theorem by the methods of Variational Analysis, adapting an idea of I. Ekeland and E. Séré [ 4 ] . 1 Introduction The classical example (x,y)\to e^{x}(\cos y,\sin y) shows that – except in dimension one – the derivative may be everywhere invertible while the function itself is invertible only locally.

arxiv-2407-20202.title: Constraints for scalars and pseudoscalars from ( g − 2 ) l \left(g-2\right)_{l} and existing e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} colliders
arxiv-2407-20202.creator: Aleksandr Pustyntsev, Marc Vanderhaeghen
arxiv-2407-20202.description: Abstract Scalars and pseudoscalars with masses in the MeV to GeV range are of interest in different extensions of the Standard Model. Such particles are often associated with dark matter, the strong CP problem and the ( g − 2 ) μ \left(g-2\right)_{\mu} anomaly.

arxiv-2411-04090.title: A Collaborative Content Moderation Framework for Toxicity Detection based on Multitask Neural Networks and Conformal Estimates of Annotation Disagreement
arxiv-2411-04090.creator: Guillermo Villate-Castillo, Javier Del Ser, Borja Sanz
arxiv-2411-04090.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Guillermo Villate-Castillo, Javier Del Ser, Borja Sanz. Content moderation typically combines the efforts of human moderators and machine learning models. However, these systems often rely on data where significant disagreement occurs during moderation, reflecting the subjective nature of toxicity perception. Rather than dismissing this disagreement as noise, we interpret it as a valuable signal that highlights the inherent ambiguity of the content—an insight missed when only the majority label is considered.

arxiv-2504-08192.title: SAEs Can Improve Unlearning: Dynamic Sparse Autoencoder Guardrails for Precision Unlearning in LLMs
arxiv-2504-08192.creator: Aashiq Muhamed, Jacopo Bonato, Mona Diab, Virginia Smith {amuhamed,mdiab,smithv}@andrew.cmu.edu, jacopo.bonato@prometeia.com
arxiv-2504-08192.description: Abstract Machine unlearning is a promising approach to improve LLM safety by removing unwanted knowledge from a trained model. However, prevailing gradient-based unlearning methods suffer from issues such as high computational costs, hyperparameter instability, poor sequential unlearning capability, vulnerability to relearning attacks, low data efficiency, and lack of interpretability.

arxiv-2507-20207.title: Directional Neutrino Bursts from Spinning and Moving Primordial Black Holes
arxiv-2507-20207.creator: Arnab Chaudhuri, Priya Mishra, Rukmani Mohanta
arxiv-2507-20207.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arnab Chaudhuri, Priya Mishra, Rukmani Mohanta. We show that primordial black holes (PBHs) with significant spin and bulk motion produce sharply collimated neutrino bursts from Hawking evaporation, arising from the interplay of spin-induced angular anisotropy and relativistic Doppler boosting. This effect shifts the neutrino spectrum into the multi-GeV to hundreds of GeV range, where atmospheric backgrounds drop steeply, and enhances the flux by orders of magnitude within a narrow forward cone.

arxiv-2511-22486.title: The Machine Learning Approach to Moment Closure Relations for Plasma: A Review
arxiv-2511-22486.creator: Samuel Burles \aff 1 \corresp, Enrico Camporeale \aff 1, \aff 2
arxiv-2511-22486.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Samuel Burles \aff 1 \corresp, Enrico Camporeale \aff 1, \aff 2. The requirement for large-scale global simulations of plasma is an ongoing challenge in both space and laboratory plasma physics. Any simulation based on a fluid model inherently requires a closure relation for the high order plasma moments. This review compiles and analyses the recent surge of machine learning approaches developing improved plasma closure models capable of capturing kinetic phenomena within plasma fluid models.

arxiv-2602-08863.title: High-brightness fiber-based Sagnac source of entangled photon pairs for multiplexed quantum networks
arxiv-2602-08863.creator: Tess Troisi, Yoann Pelet, Romain Dalidet, Gregory Sauder, Olivier Alibart, Sébastien Tanzilli, Anthony Martin
arxiv-2602-08863.description: Abstract A fully fibered source of entangled photon pairs based on a nonlinear Sagnac interferometer is reported. Operating at telecom wavelengths, the source relies exclusively on standard fiber-optic components and periodically poled lithium niobate (PPLN) waveguides, resulting in a compact, robust, and field-deployable architecture.

pmc-10564408.title: Single-cell and bulk sequencing analyses reveal the immune suppressive role of PTPN6 in glioblastoma
pmc-10564408.creator: Xiaonan Zhang, Jie Chen, Ming Zhang, Saisai Liu, Tao Wang, Tianyu Wu, Baiqing Li, Shidi Zhao, Hongtao Wang, Li Li, Chun Wang, Li Huang
pmc-10564408.description: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly malignant brain cancer with a poor prognosis despite standard treatments. This investigation aimed to explore the feasibility of PTPN6 to combat GBM with immunotherapy. Our study employed a comprehensive analysis of publicly available datasets and functional experiments to assess PTPN6 gene expression, prognostic value, and related immune characteristics in glioma.

pmc-11434858.title: A Comprehensive Review of Silver and Gold Nanoparticles as Effective Antibacterial Agents
pmc-11434858.creator: Ricardo Aguilar-Garay, Luis F. Lara-Ortiz, Maximiliano Campos-López, Dafne E. Gonzalez-Rodriguez, Margoth M. Gamboa-Lugo, Jorge A. Mendoza-Pérez, Álvaro Anzueto-Ríos, Dulce E. Nicolás-Álvarez
pmc-11434858.description: The increasing threat from antibiotic-resistant bacteria has necessitated the development of novel methods to counter bacterial infections. In this context, the application of metallic nanoparticles (NPs), especially gold (Au) and silver (Ag), has emerged as a promising strategy due to their remarkable antibacterial properties.

pmc-11464587.title: Clinicopathological, immunohistochemical and therapeutic approaches on survival in patients with epithelioid glioblastoma: Institutional experience in the management of 58 patients
pmc-11464587.creator: Meng-nan Sun, Shao-qun Li, Yao Guo, Jiang-fen Zhou, Dan-dan Fu, Xiao-yu Hua, Xiao-jun Yu, Ming-yao Lai, Lin-bo Cai, Chang-zheng Shi
pmc-11464587.description: Epithelioid glioblastoma (Ep-GBM) is a rare variant of glioblastoma characterized by a high recurrence rate and poor prognosis. Currently, there is no established standard treatment for Ep-GBM. Therefore, we identified 58 Ep-GBM cases to investigate these characteristics and identify the possible prognostic factors of survival. There were 30 male and 28 female patients with a median age of 39 years.

pmc-11530831.title: Advances and challenges in the use of liquid biopsy in gynaecological oncology
pmc-11530831.creator: Yingfeng Zhang, Libi Tian
pmc-11530831.description: Ovarian cancer, endometrial cancer, and cervical cancer are the three primary gynaecological cancers that pose a significant threat to women's health on a global scale. Enhancing global cancer survival rates necessitates advancements in illness detection and monitoring, with the goal of improving early diagnosis and prognostication of disease recurrence.

pmc-12383249.title: Multidecadal decoupling between coral calcifying fluid and seawater saturation states
pmc-12383249.creator: Jessica C. Hankins, Thomas M. DeCarlo
pmc-12383249.description: Ocean acidification poses a threat to coral skeleton formation via reductions in the saturation state of aragonite (ΩAr) in seawater. Given that corals precipitate their skeletons from a calcifying fluid supplied by seawater, reductions in seawater ΩAr should, in theory, confound calcification.

pmc-12510045.title: Nucleotide motif-guided selection of plasma microRNA biomarkers in trauma
pmc-12510045.creator: Boyang Ren, Ruoxing Li, Chien-Yu Lin, Chanhee Park, Sheng Wang, Andrew O Suen, John Kessler, Shiming Yang, Rosemary Kozar, Lin Zou, Brittney Williams, Ziyi Li, Peter Hu, Wei Chao
pmc-12510045.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). SummaryTrauma remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in part due to complex pathophysiological responses. Yet our abilities to predict these changes are limited. Plasma miRNAs have been proposed as DAMPs that drive immune response and organ injury. Here, we test a panel of plasma miRNAs—selected based on next-generation sequencing and nucleotide motifs identified via a machine-learning algorithm—for their abilities to predict subclinical pathophysiological injuries.

Introduction:Osteoarthritis (OA) of the knee is a prevalent degenerative condition influenced by inflammatory processes. Vitamin D possesses immunomodulatory properties that could potentially impact cytokine expression, notably interleukin (IL)-6 and -10, in osteoarthritic pathology.

pmc-13669207.title: PDHA1 Hyperactivation‐Mediated Glucose Metabolism Reprogramming Fuels Neutrophil NETosis and Promotes Acute Lung Injury
pmc-13669207.creator: Yu‐Biao Liu, Wen‐Jing Zhong, Chen‐Yu Zhang, Meng‐Rui Chen, Nan‐Shi‐Yu Yang, Han‐Xi Sha, Yan‐Ling Qiu, Hui Chen, Jin‐Tong Yang, Li‐Ying Liang, Jian‐Bing Xiong, Shao‐Kun Liu, Cha‐Xiang Guan, Jia‐Xi Duan, Yong Zhou
pmc-13669207.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, termed NETosis, is a key driver of lung tissue injury in acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome (ALI/ARDS). However, the precise mechanisms that trigger neutrophil NETosis remain incompletely understood. Here, we observed that neutrophils from both ALI mice and ARDS patients exhibited NETosis alongside a pronounced selective metabolic shift, characterized by enhanced oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and attenuated glycolytic activity.
